This information is intended for use by healthcare providers, public health professionals, and those organizing and implementing testing in non-healthcare settings. Viral tests , including nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) and PCR tests, as well as antigen tests, are used as diagnostic tests to detect current infection with SARS-CoV-2, determine the need for prevention measures, and inform a person's medical care. Viral tests Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) are highly sensitive and highly specific tests that detect one or more viral ribonucleic acid (RNA) genes. PCR tests are the most common type of NAAT used for COVID-19 testing. Viral RNA may stay in a person's body for up to 90 days after they test positive. From the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific Ocean, the Pacific Northwest Trail is a unique hiking experience, offering a variety of back-country scenery and outdoor adventure. The 1200-mile Pacific Northwest Trail, running from the Continental Divide to the Pacific Ocean, ranks among the most scenic trails in the world. The PNT crosses 3 National Parks and 7 National Forests, and ends at the Pacific Ocean, on Washington's Olympic Peninsula. On Bureau of Land Management (BLM) lands, this trail meanders through areas rich in Native American and Pioneer history, along a historic railroad grade deep in the canyon of the Similkameen River, and high above the shores of Lake Chopaka, in the heart of the Okanogan highlands of northern Washington. Asif Merchant was found guilty in March of attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire after trying to hire hitmen to kill Trump, former President Joe Biden, and former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley. The hitmen were instead undercover FBI agents. In court, he said he was acting under the direction of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to avenge the 2020 US assassination of Qasem Soleimani, Iran's topmost military commander. New York US federal judge Eric Ross Komitee sentenced Merchant on Tuesday to 330 months (27 years and six months) in prison, months after a jury handed its guilty verdict. Although other US officials were potential targets, the assassination plot was largely focused on Trump because he was president at the time Soleimani was killed. SCIENCE LAELAPS Paleo Profile: Wucaiwan’s Ornamented Horned Face By Riley Black Published January 22, 2016 • 4 min read The ceratopsians are among our favorite dinosaurs. These great horned herbivores included Triceratops , Styracosaurus , and Pentaceratops in their ranks, as well as celebrated newcomers like Nasutoceratops . But these were only some of the largest and last of their kind. A new find, reported by paleontologist Genglu Han and colleagues, is a reminder that ceratopsians started off small. The new dinosaur, found in the Late Jurassic rock of northwestern China, has been named Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis by the researchers. And while it looked relatively similar to another early horned dinosaur found in the same formation, Yinlong downsi , the skull pieces of Hualianceratops justify its identification as something different. And this has some important implications for the way horned dinosaurs evolved. The new family tree of early ceratopsians proposed by Han and coauthors suggests that horned dinosaurs were undoing a rapid radiation right after they stepped onto the evolutionary stage. Panteón Rococó: Tiny Desk Concert October 1, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Michael Zamora/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Panteón Rococó has been at the forefront of Mexican ska for over three decades. With lyrics that stare down its country's toughest sociopolitical struggles, the band's skankin' grooves slide easily between cumbia and Afro-Caribbean rhythms. At El Tiny, the music and the message is heard loud and clear. After "Arreglame el Alma," lead singer Dr. Shenka greets the crowd and launches into "1993…," a devastating testimonial about the countless desaparecidos (missing) throughout Mexico. For the uninitiated, it might seem counterintuitive for such a sensitive subject to be set to upbeat music. But Panteón Rococó's frenetic energy allows for an emotional and physical release of the despair and hopelessness of daily life that can beset modern Mexico. And when surrounded by others hopping up and down, singing songs of resistance, you're no longer alone. pages.text: Paradata Paradata Skip Navigation Paradata About Working Papers About About Working Papers About What is paradata? Paradata is a term used to describe data generated as a by-product of the data collection process. Types of paradata vary from contact attempt history records for interviewer-assisted operations, to form tracing using tracking numbers in mail surveys, to keystroke or mouse-click history for internet self-response surveys. Because paradata are a by-product of a given data collection operation, the format, layout and content of paradata are a function of the system that generated the data. Integrating these data requires a variety of software and statistical tools. These challenges are worth overcoming, however, as paradata can be informative about the progress, cost and quality of both particular data collection operations and overall survey management. Why does the Census Bureau need paradata? Nonresponse in federal surveys increasing as budgets for data collection are decreasing. In order to gather and provide accurate information on the U.S. population and economy in a cost-effective manner, we need to utilize our resources efficiently. Paradata can help us identify potential areas of improvement, implement changes, and then evaluate the effect of those changes. Paradata are used for a variety of reasons across the Bureau, in order to: Measure and limit contact burden in our federal surveys. Time reminder mailings and contacts based on outgoing and incoming mail tracking. Selectively assign data collection features, such as incentives, shorter questionnaires

Parents: Help Children Fight Flu Sept. 17, 2024 What to know Influenza (flu) is a contagious respiratory disease caused by influenza viruses. Flu can be more dangerous than the common cold for children. Each year, flu places a large burden on the health and well-being of children and their families. Annual flu vaccination offers the best protection against flu and its potentially serious complications in children. Parents can help children fight flu by getting themselves and their children vaccinated against flu each year. Overview Children younger than 5 years old—especially those younger than 2—and children of any age with certain chronic health conditions, like asthma and diabetes, are at higher risk of developing potentially serious flu complications. Because these groups of children are at higher risk, it is especially important that they get a seasonal flu vaccine to help prevent flu, and to reduce their risk of being hospitalized or dying from flu if they do get sick. How can I reduce my exposure to PM? What is PM, and how does it get into the air? Size comparisons for PM particles PM stands for particulate matter (also called particle pollution): the term for a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets found in the air. Some particles, such as dust, dirt, soot, or smoke, are large or dark enough to be seen with the naked eye. Others are so small they can only be detected using an electron microscope. Particle pollution includes: PM 10 : inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 10 micrometers and smaller; and PM 2.5 : fine inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 2.5 micrometers and smaller. How small is 2.5 micrometers? Think about a single hair from your head. The average human hair is about 70 micrometers in diameter – making it 30 times larger than the largest fine particle. Sources of PM These particles come in many sizes and shapes and can be made up of hundreds of different chemicals. pages.text: Partner With SIS Partner With SIS Skip Navigation Within Statistics in Schools Partner With SIS The U.S. Census Bureau invites teachers and educational organizations to partner with the agency to promote the Statistics in Schools (SIS) program. Partner support makes it possible for more students to benefit from SIS resources that expand their ability to understand and use statistics in a data-driven world. Become an SIS Ambassador About: The Statistics in Schools (SIS) Ambassador Program is a collaborative effort by educators, librarians, and the Census Bureau to discuss and determine the needs of teachers and students in today’s data-driven world and provide educators with real-life tools and data to boost the statistical literacy of K-12 students. Commitment: Ambassadors are encouraged to promote use of SIS materials and to participate in select SIS virtual events and special initiatives – an estimated 5-10 hours/school year. Perks: Being an ambassador gives you a voice in the development of new SIS products and opens the door to customized virtual field trips and sessions with Census Bureau statisticians ready to field your questions about real data. The role also provides opportunities to network with other educators across the country and learn innovative ways to bring census statistics into the classroom. Plus, ambassadors receive a digital badge and other potential national recognition opportunities. Contact us at [email protected] to learn how to become an SIS ambassador. pages.text: Pat Cummins calls Usman Khawaja sandpaper claims 'wrong' and 'nonsense' - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Pat Cummins was named Australia Test captain in 2021 By Stephan Shemilt Cricket Correspondent Published 12 November 2026 Updated 13 November 2026 Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Figure caption, Complete and utter nonsense - Cummins Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague". McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed. But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers. It comes ahead of a long-awaited review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, which will recommend on Tuesday that under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work. His report is also expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. pages.text: Peace Corps Volunteers | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Peace Corps Volunteers Federal Employees’ Compensation Program A Peace Corps Volunteer who sustains an injury or illness in performance of their Peace Corps service may be entitled to benefits under the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA). The FECA, administered by the Department's Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (OWCP), provides medical, wage loss and other compensation benefits for Peace Corps Volunteers who sustain injury or illness while in the performance of duty. Peace Corps Volunteers are considered to be in the performance of duty while abroad during the period of Peace Corps service for purposes of FECA coverage. An injury sustained outside the United States is deemed proximately caused by such service, unless the injury or illness was caused by willful misconduct, intention to bring about injury or death, or intoxication. FECA benefits may also be provided for an injury or illness present prior to entering Peace Corps service, if evidence supports that Peace Corps service contributed to a worsening of the condition. The Peace Corps provides medical and dental care that covers all related expenses during service, including preventative care and issues incurred during training period. Until you are separated from the Peace Corps, you are encouraged to seek medical and dental care from the Peace Corps . Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Pechuck Lookout In the early 20th century, a growing concern for fire protection in forested areas resulted in the construction of lookouts with wide views throughout the Pacific Northwest. Located on the Table Rock Trail, within the BLM Northwest Oregon District boundary, the Pechuck Lookout was established in 1918, at an elevation of 4,338 feet. Originally, the lookout consisted only of a primitive fire detection rangefinder; and some years later, in the early 1930s, a small stone and wood cabin was built. The Pechuck Lookout, also known as a cupola, was built by John Oblack, a Czechoslovakian from Molalla with help from an unknown stone mason from Portland. The cupola-type lookout was built primarily with native stone from sources nearby and the lower story served as the living quarters for hearty individuals staffing the fire lookout. The upper story has windows on all four sides and provides a 360-degree view of the surrounding landscape. Until 1932, the only access to the lookout site was by way of the Table Rock Trail through what is now Table Rock Wilderness. People at Increased Risk for Food Poisoning Jan. 31, 2025 Key points Certain groups of people are at higher risk for severe illness from foodborne illness. Higher risk groups include people who are 65 and older, children under 5, people with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women. People at increased risk Anyone can get food poisoning, but certain groups of people are more likely to get very sick from food poisoning. For these people, their body may not be able to fight germs and sickness as effectively. It's especially important to take steps to prevent food poisoning if you or someone you care for belong to one of the groups below. People 65 and older People aged 65 and older are at increased risk for food poisoning. As people age, their immune systems and organs don't recognize and get rid of harmful germs as well as they once did. This increases the chance they'll get sick from food poisoning. Nearly half of people aged 65 and older who have a lab-confirmed foodborne illness from Salmonella , Campylobacter , Listeria or E. coli are hospitalized. January 30, 2025 People at Increased Risk for Illness from Animals What to know Anyone can get sick from germs animals can carry, but some people are more likely to get sick and have more serious illness. Riskier animals include rodents, reptiles, amphibians, and poultry. These people don't need to avoid all contact with animals but should be aware of the risks and take steps to protect themselves. High-risk animals Turtles can carry germs that can make some people very sick. These animals are more likely to carry germs that can make people sick: Reptiles and amphibians (lizards, snakes, turtles, frogs) Backyard poultry (chickens, ducks, turkeys, geese) Rodents (hamsters, guinea pigs, rats, mice, and other small rodents) Exotic pets (monkeys and other wild animals) Even animals that look clean and healthy can carry harmful germs, and areas where animals live or roam can be contaminated – you don’t have to touch an animal to get sick. The depth and extent of this “permafrost” varies by location, depending on average air temperatures, soil types, topography, and surface vegetation. Frozen ground is stable, providing a solid foundation for roads and buildings. Permafrost is also impermeable, so water pools on the surface instead of seeping through the soil, and creates a landscape dotted with many small lakes. The shorter and warmer winters are affecting permafrost. – Dave Swanson, Fairbanks Rising temperatures are melting this frozen ground and forever altering the landscape. Without this solid foundation, roads and buildings sink into the softer, non-frozen ground. Sinkholes and slumpages form when their frozen supportive underground layers thaw. Some people use PAS to carry out activities of daily living. Depending on the individual, such activities might include getting up and ready for work, bathing, dressing, cooking, cleaning, or running errands. Some people also use PAS in the workplace. Examples of workplace PAS vary, but may involve activities such as retrieving materials out of reach or providing travel assistance for an employee with a mobility impairment; helping an employee with a cognitive disability in decision-making; reading printed materials to an employee who is visually impaired; or ensuring a sign language interpreter is present during meetings for an employee who is deaf. Whether at home or work, PAS can be essential to employment success. Recognizing this, ODEP works to expand and raise awareness of employment-related PAS options. Meeting the needs of people on and off the job raises important policy issues for federal and state governments, service providers, and employers, as well as people with disabilities themselves. Pertussis CHIM Biorepository Dec. 2, 2025 Key points Scientists recently developed a pertussis controlled human infection model (pertussis CHIM). The aim was to build a foundation for and accelerate development and licensure of next-generation pertussis vaccines in the United States. Biological samples from this pertussis CHIM are available for researchers. Request samples by following the application process. Overview The first North American pertussis CHIM study began enrolling participants in July 2022. The objective of this study was to establish a pertussis CHIM. History In 2010, a paper map by 3dShapes was digitized and imported, to map landuse in Nederland. The import project was well conducted and properly documented in the OSM-wiki. This was a major step in filling in the space on OSM. Some problems remained after import, to be dealt with later. For instance, where trees had been planted in multiple rows, it was imported as an orchard. As a result, our motorways were suddenly lined with orchards, on OSM-based maps. This has been fixed by organized mappings. Another example: the paper map had a tile grid of thin black lines. These lines were seen as cut lines, resulting in unnecessary and awkward splits of the imported areas. The import procedure did detect this problem, but couldn’t automate a fix, so this was left to the future mappers. It took 15 years before a crazy mapper got rid of this in a solo project lasting 2 months. Guess who? The issue Not much of a problem, more of an annoyance, really: All polygons were tagged with “source=3dShapes”. A significant part of the polygons still carry this source tag. pages.text: Peter Storey: Former Arsenal and England midfielder dies aged 81 - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Peter Storey won 19 caps for England Published 17 November 2026 Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. "We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund." Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield. He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions. Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72. He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired. Phil Kangas Deputy Director, Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) Phil Kangas is the Deputy Director of the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), focusing on the Office's operations and mission delivery. He previously served as the Acting Deputy Director and Division Director for Outreach and Business Development (OBD), where he led efforts to source quality project applications. Prior to joining DOE, Mr. Kangas spent 25 years in the private sector as a management consultant, including a 20+ year career at Grant Thornton LLP, where he led the firm’s National Energy Advisory practice for clients in the natural resources, mining, and renewables sectors. He also led the federal sciences portfolio for work delivered at DOE, Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), National Science Foundation (NSF), and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Mr. Kangas earned a Bachelor of Arts in History and Political Science from John Carroll University and a Master of Public Administration from Syracuse University’s Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs.
